title: Hygon DCU gfx938 is measurable hardware for the AMD naming sequence, and closes F-2026-09-13-006's last step

evidence.note: Read-only survey from macOS through 'ssh bw1100', inside a transient container from harbor.sourcefind.cn:5443/dcu/admin/base/custom:vllm0.29.0-ubuntu22.04-dtk26.04-py3.10-20260831-qwen3.8flashnext with /opt/dtk/env.sh sourced. rocminfo.txt is the full device capture; probe-log.txt holds the Triton backend/driver probe, an ahead-of-time elementwise compile, an FP16 tl.dot compile and the hipcc resource-usage probe, with the probe scripts beside them. No kernel was dispatched, no device was written to, and no correctness or performance claim is made.

Timing and L2 survey on one BW1101 agent. torch.cuda.Event empty-interval overhead min 8.48 us / median 9.28 us against 3-7 us kernels, so events are not the CUPTI peer. rocprofv2 --kernel-trace writes per-dispatch nanosecond Start_Timestamp/End_Timestamp plus GRD, WGR, LDS, SCR, Arch_VGPR, ACCUM_VGPR, SGPR and Wave_Size; hipprof --hip-trace is a second source at 10 ns granularity; rocprofv3 is absent. L2 flush has no HIP API and is a 256 MiB zero_() costing 243.8 us; its measured effect on torch.mul is 1.24x at 1 MiB buffers, 1.12x at 2 MiB and 1.00x at and above 4 MiB, where input and output together meet the 8 MiB L2. Streaming bandwidth saturates near 1.76 TB/s. Two negative results and one superseded 1.96x figure caused by a kernel-name filter that also matched PyTorch's fill kernel are retained in the same log. Exploratory: no Workload, no oracle, no claim.

The Compiler's own path lowered corpus case gfx938-rmsnorm-b8-smoke and compiled it in the container through compile_triton to an hsaco: 256 threads per CTA (4 slots x 64), 512 dynamic shared bytes, 134 VGPRs, no scratch, source_sha256 e7406e09e0e4b866d9721d5df27e8f1cc845abc7dd37696391ab9220962eb2c4, which is the same lowering digest the Corpus Gate pins for that case. Running the emitted host wrapper against a PyTorch reference on one BW1101 matched at rtol=2e-5, atol=2e-6 across primary, zeros, near-zero, alternating-sign and mixed-magnitude inputs, maximum absolute error 3.8e-6. A correctness check with no Workload Contract, frozen oracle, tolerance contract or Executor; it establishes nothing about performance.

observation: rocminfo inside the container reports eight agents named gfx938, marketing name BW1101, vendor C-3000, device type HCU, ISA amdgcn-amd-amdhsa--gfx938:sramecc+:xnack-, wavefront size 64, workgroup max 1024 threads, 64 KiB GROUP segment, 64 compute units with 4 SIMDs each, 40 max waves per CU, 32 KiB L1, 8 MiB L2 and ~144 GiB of device memory. It reports no registers-per-CU figure. Triton 3.6.0 registers backends amd, hcu and nvidia; the active driver is triton.backends.hcu.driver and reports GPUTarget(backend='hip', arch='gfx938', warp_size=64). ASTSource plus triton.compile against that explicit GPUTarget succeeds in a container with neither /dev/kfd nor /dev/dri, where Triton itself reports 0 active drivers, so the offline-compilation property survives the port. Four CUDA commitments in toolchain.compile_triton do not: cuda_architecture refuses any non-sm target and feeds GPUTarget('cuda', architecture, 32); the fixed artifact roles source/ttir/ttgir/llir/ptx/cubin are measured here as source/ttir/ttgir/llir/amdgcn/hsaco; the exact-output check is a '.target sm_XXX' PTX regex where the DCU peer is the amdhsa.target line in the amdgcn text; and metadata.global_scratch_size is absent on the hcu metadata object, so the auxiliary-scratch refusal would raise AttributeError instead of refusing. inspect_triton_resources shells out to cuobjdump, which is absent, as are roc-obj and llvm-objdump; the amdgcn text Triton already returns carries .vgpr_count, .sgpr_count, .group_segment_fixed_size and .private_segment_fixed_size, measured as VGPR 95, SGPR 18, static LDS 0 and scratch 0 on a 64x64x32 FP16 tl.dot, whose metadata.shared is 16384 -- the same static-zero/dynamic-allocation trap AGENTS.md records for gemm-bias-b1-smoke. That tl.dot lowers to v_mmac_f32_16x16x16_f16 and to no v_mfma instruction, and the hcu metadata carries enable_v_mmac_cluster, mmac_layout_force and empty_arrive_after_mmac, so this is not a relabelled CDNA part and its instruction contracts cannot be borrowed from an MFMA or NVIDIA vocabulary. Underneath all of it, Target.warp_size is a hard-coded 32 with no Target-document field behind it, read by the hardware-conformance thread-extent, register-budget and shared-memory derivations, by residency and profile thread counts, and by the CuTe-DSL THREADS_PER_CTA emission; every one of them is wrong by a factor of two at wavefront 64. Separately, hipcc (dcc 25.10.0 / clang 17) compiles for --offload-arch=gfx938 and -Rpass-analysis=kernel-resource-usage reports SGPRs, VGPRs, ScratchSize bytes/lane, LDS bytes/block, occupancy waves/SIMD and both spill counts at compile time, which is the offline peer of the -Xptxas=-v contract native_cuda already relies on. Two further facts were settled after the initial survey. hipGetDeviceProperties reports maxSharedMemoryPerMultiProcessor 65536, contradicting torch.cuda.get_device_properties' 4194304, and hipcc -Rpass-analysis=kernel-resource-usage confirms 64 KiB of LDS per compute unit by reporting 10, 8, 4, 2 and 1 waves/SIMD for one 256-thread workgroup as declared LDS rises 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 KiB, so a full occupancy block is declarable and the PyTorch figure is not used. Separately, HIPOptions has no maxnreg field and Triton's option parser drops an unknown key without raising, so the per-thread register cap the emitter attaches for CUDA is accepted on this route and never applied. Submitted under 2026-09-15 after a pull: F-2026-09-14-001 through -005 were already allocated to unrelated work by parallel sessions, and 2026-09-15-001 with them. F-2026-09-13-006 owns the AMD sequence and records that 'no AMD device measurement is available to this project'; that is the sentence this finding retires. Its steps 1 to 3 are now in place -- warp_size upstream in Compiler v81, vendor identity and warpgroup width declared and the synthetic third-vendor neutrality fixture installed in the v83 draft -- so the gfx938 document is the data addition that finding says it should be, rather than a sixth target arriving ahead of the shared-layer work.
proposed_change: Land gfx938 as the first AMD Target on the declared-vendor schema: vendor amd, warp_size 64, no compute_capability, no warpgroup width, device-observed limits and occupancy, no peak and no instruction contracts. Route Triton's compilation on the declared target -- GPUTarget, artifact roles, exact-target text and the scratch fields the route's backend actually defines -- and read allocation from the .amdgpu_metadata note rather than the absent cuobjdump. Refuse a declared per-thread register budget on this route, because Triton's HIPOptions has no maxnreg field and its option parser drops an unknown key without raising. Keep one LoweringBackend member for one unchanged mechanism and let the Triton backend module own which exact targets it admits; whether AGENTS.md's registration rule wants a member anyway is a reading for the reviewer. Update the exact-target pin as the deliberate act that pin exists for.
verification_plan: Corpus Gate 150/150 with all 147 pre-existing expectations unchanged and three gfx938 cases adopted separately; gfx938-wave64-thread-extent is one Schedule that is lowering-eligible on sm_100a at 1024 threads and refused on gfx938 at 2048. On device, the lowered gfx938-rmsnorm-b8-smoke compiles to an hsaco at 256 threads per CTA and matches a PyTorch reference across five input distributions at 3.8e-6 maximum absolute error, and all 27 task baselines gfx938 admits compile. None of that is an Evaluation: there is no Workload Contract, frozen oracle or Executor behind any of it, and F-2026-09-15-003 is why there cannot be. Remaining: an independent ADR 0052 review and a released Compiler successor; an Executor successor, since this change also touches evaluation/artifacts.py and lab/executor.py; and a DCU Executor, which capture_executor_host.py cannot yet produce because --kind admits only cuda and metal. Report gfx938 timing-model coverage as unavailable throughout.
